category: B2B industrial supplies (precision bearings & motion components)
title: Pune bearings supplier ditched broad demand-gen and won 11 plant accounts with account-based LinkedIn
content: SITUATION: A Pune supplier of precision linear bearings and motion components had a tiny, countable TAM — ~320 OEM plants across Pune, Chakan and Coimbatore that actually spec their class of part. The buy ran 7-9 months through a maintenance engineer, then a purchase manager. They were burning ₹1.8L/month on Google Search and Meta for 140 leads at ₹1,290 CPL, but ~80% were students, traders or wrong-spec hobbyists — just two qualified RFQs that whole quarter. ACTION: They killed broad demand-gen. They built a named list of all 320 plants, mapped 540 maintenance and procurement decision-makers in LinkedIn Sales Navigator (₹5,300/month), and ran ₹1.4L/month of account-based LinkedIn ads plus personal connection requests against only those names. Content was trade-specific — load-rating calculators, ISO 281 life guides, MTBF field notes — not 'we supply quality parts.' Warm replies moved to WhatsApp for drawings and quotes, with specs confirmed over email. OUTCOME: Over 9 months CPL fell to ₹740 but on real buyers: 38 qualified RFQs, 11 plant accounts closed worth ₹2.6Cr, at a blended CAC of ₹1.1L against a ₹24L average account value. LESSON: When your TAM fits on a spreadsheet, stop buying reach. Name every account, reach the two humans who actually sign off, and let technical-depth content do the qualifying for you.
lesson: When your TAM is small enough to list on a spreadsheet, broad demand-gen wastes budget on the wrong audience. Name every account, target the 2-3 people who actually sign off, and use technical-depth content (calculators, standards, field data — not 'quality parts' claims) to self-qualify a long, multi-stakeholder buy.
